subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output needs

Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output needs

Hi Sarah & Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Let me know if I mis-stated anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Agent output is currently too inconsistent for downstream processing (schema drift, missing fields).
- Your orchestrator (LangChain + internal router) struggles with retries and error semantics when functions fail.
- High CPU cost from post-processing/normalization of LLM outputs; need deterministic formatting to simplify ingestion.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Orchestration: LangChain + homegrown agency layer
- Models: mix of hosted open models and in-house tuned variants
- Consumers: real-time ingestion into event pipeline (Kafka) and a downstream validation service

Success criteria you called out (for an initial POC):
1) Deterministic JSON output for 95% of prompts (schema validation pass rate)
2) Clear function-calling / tool-calling semantics (success/failure statuses surfaced in response)
3) Latency <= 350ms p50 for the typical 300-token prompts when running on Dedicated capacity
4) Ops visibility: token-level cost and per-route error rates surfaced in Console

What Redwood can deliver for the POC (high level):
- Function/tool-calling primitives that return structured JSON with explicit error fields and consistent typing.
- Support for custom JSON schemas (we can validate model output server-side and fallback to safe defaults).
- Agent workflows: deterministic step ordering, retry policies, and deterministic sampling configs for predictable outputs.
- Reference doc attached: redwood_function_calling_reference.pdf

Immediate next steps:
- We’d like your sample JSON schema for the primary endpoint (can you send a canonical example of what the downstream consumer expects?).
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) — propose Thu 4/16 10:00am PT or Fri 4/17 11:00am PT.
- We’ll draft a mutual action plan + scope (attached: mutual_action_plan.pdf).

Thanks — I’ll follow up after you share the sample schema.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — this looks accurate. Couple of clarifications and I attached a small schema example (acme_sample_output_schema.json) so you can see our exact expectations.

Clarifications:
- Deterministic output: we don’t need absolute determinism for all prompts, but we need the top-level structure and required fields to be present every time so our downstream validator can accept the payload without human intervention.
- Error semantics: when a tool call fails we need a consistent error object with machine-readable codes and a soft-fail path (i.e., the agent can continue with degraded capabilities).
- Validation tolerance: if the model returns unknown enum values we prefer a mapped fallback value rather than reject the message outright.

Attached: acme_sample_output_schema.json — it’s the schema our ingestion expects for the ‘extract_entities’ endpoint.

Preferred deep-dive time: Thu 4/16 10:00am PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite with an agenda and any relevant pre-reads.

Best,

Hi Sarah — great to meet you earlier (virtually). I’m Marissa on the Solutions team — looping in a few technical details so we can hit the ground running in the deep-dive.

Notes on approach:
1) Schema validation + model-safety layer: we can accept your acme_sample_output_schema.json server-side and run validation immediately after generation. If validation fails, we can either: (a) trigger a constrained re-generation with stricter decode settings, or (b) return a canonical error object with the failure reasons. We’ll plan the behavior during the POC.

2) Function/tool-calling surface: Redwood’s function-calling returns a JSON envelope with: 
   - output: the payload matching your schema (when successful)
   - tool_calls: recorded calls with timestamps and tool response bodies
   - status: OK | PARTIAL | ERROR
   - error: { code, message, retriable }

3) Deterministic formatting: two levers we typically use — (A) constrained sampling + temperature=0 for fields that must be deterministic, (B) post-generation canonicalizers that map enums/typings to canonical values. Both are supported in Dedicated.

4) Agent workflows / retries: we can encode retry policies as first-class config (max_retries, backoff_ms, fallback_tool). For example, if a DB lookup tool fails, you can set a fallback to return an empty array + error code rather than blocking the agent.

Ask from your side before the deep-dive:
- Confirm which fields in acme_sample_output_schema.json are required vs optional (if you can mark them inline or return a small table, that’ll speed up the POC design).
- Share an example prompt set (3–5 prompts) that represent typical user traffic.

I’ve dropped a short pre-read in our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleSharedDrive and attached a reference PDF for our function-calling contract (redwood_function_calling_reference.pdf).

I’ll be on the Thu 4/16 10:00am PT call — Jordan, can you send the invite with a calendar link?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
